messages.subject: Trap covariates + rsfDF covariates?
parts:
Hello all,

I'm working with a remote camera dataset that has accompanying telemetry data. Right now the models I'm running are set to RSF = F, but I'm interested in adding covariates to an rsfDF. However, I'm wondering is it possible to run models with spatial covariates on the trap locations that cannot also be included in the rsfDF? For example trap covariates like remote camera model used, or the recreation level on the trail where the camera was set - things that matter for traps but aren't applicable to the full rsfDF. In the few tests I've done these kinds of models don't work, I'm not sure if I'm attempting something that isn't correct/possible or maybe coding something incorrectly. 

Thank you!
Greta

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: [oscr] Trap covariates + rsfDF covariates?
parts: Hi Joël, does this covariate vary by trap or just occasion?  If the former, you'd need to have unique values for all pixels in your rsfDF to reflect the spatial variation.  I assume it's more likely that temperature varied over time the same for every trap, in which case you could simply put a single value in the rsfDF that corresponds to the mean (x = 0, if standardized).  Technically it shouldn't matter what that value is so long as it's the same for every pixel.  This way, the model is acknowledging variation by occasion for all traps that is constant across space and, thus, should not interfere with the RSF.  Let me know if that works!

Le mardi 12 octobre 2021 à 08:16:14 UTC-4, danl...@gmail.com a écrit :
Hi Joël, does this covariate vary by trap or just occasion?  If the former, you'd need to have unique values for all pixels in your rsfDF to reflect the spatial variation.  I assume it's more likely that temperature varied over time the same for every trap, in which case you could simply put a single value in the rsfDF that corresponds to the mean (x = 0, if standardized).  Technically it shouldn't matter what that value is so long as it's the same for every pixel.  This way, the model is acknowledging variation by occasion for all traps that is constant across space and, thus, should not interfere with the RSF.  Let me know if that works!
